recharge_pit: Clean the first-flush filter and mesh before monsoon (May–June).
Remove leaves and silt from the pit top and inlet chamber.
Replace the top sand layer if water stands for more than a day after rain.
Check the pit cover is intact so children and animals are safe.
recharge_trench: Clean the first-flush filter and mesh before monsoon (May–June).
Clear leaves and silt along the trench surface.
Replace the top sand/gravel layer if water stands after rain.
storage_tank: Clean the first-flush filter and mesh before monsoon (May–June).
Wash the tank once a year and keep the lid closed (mosquito safety).
Check the overflow pipe is clear and leads to a drain or pit.

needs_cleaning.filter: Open the filter, wash the mesh and remove trapped leaves and silt before the next rain.
needs_cleaning.pit: Scoop out leaves and silt from the pit top and inlet; replace the top sand layer if it is caked.
needs_cleaning.gutter: Clear leaves and debris from the gutter and downpipe so rain reaches the filter.
needs_cleaning.tank: Drain and scrub the tank, clean the inlet mesh and keep the lid closed.
needs_cleaning.unknown: Clean the filter mesh and inlet, and remove leaves and silt before the monsoon.

broken.filter: The filter looks damaged — replace the mesh or filter unit before the monsoon.
broken.pit: The pit or its cover looks damaged — get a mason to repair it so water can soak in safely.
broken.gutter: The gutter or pipe looks broken — repair the joint or replace the section so water isn't lost.
broken.tank: The tank looks cracked or leaking — repair or replace it before the monsoon.
broken.unknown: Part of the system looks damaged — get it repaired before the monsoon.

vision._note: Location check: a 'healthy' photo verifies a plan only if taken within max_photo_distance_m (+ up to max_accuracy_allowance_m of GPS uncertainty) of the plan's location, within max_capture_age_minutes.

simulation._note: 31 July 2024: an intense evening downpour over Delhi. Open-Meteo's archive gives 116 mm at Lodhi Road, 41 mm in Dwarka, 59 mm in Rohini and 280 mm over east and south-east Delhi (Mayur Vihar, Lajpat Nagar) for that day — the heaviest day in the archive for Lodhi Road since 2022. daily_cycles: a pit or tank empties (soaks away or is used) and refills about 3 times across a day of bursts; this is an assumption, not a measured figure.

contaminationSourceNearby.reason_text: A septic tank, soak pit or sewer line nearby could let dirty water reach the groundwater through a recharge pit.
contaminationSourceNearby.check_text: Check where your septic tank, soak pit and sewer line run before choosing where to dig. Ask a qualified plumber or the Jal Board how far a recharge pit must be from them.

waterloggingArea.reason_text: In an area that waterlogs, the ground is already full, so a recharge pit can overflow and push dirty street water back in.
waterloggingArea.check_text: Check whether your street or compound floods in heavy rain. If it does, a storage tank is usually the safer choice; confirm with the Jal Board.

pitNearFoundation.reason_text: Soaking water into the ground right next to the foundation can weaken it or cause damp in the walls.
pitNearFoundation.check_text: Check how close the open ground is to your building's foundation. Ask a structural engineer or qualified plumber before digging near it.

feasibility._source: Wording only; no official setback distances are cited because none were verified for this project. Users are directed to a qualified plumber or the Delhi Jal Board.

dashboard._note: Plans in these wards (e.g. created by scripts/warm.sh) are left out of dashboard figures.

water_balance._note: use_litres_per_person_per_day: rainwater a household draws from a tank for washing, toilets and garden (same figure used to size tanks). water_price_inr_per_kl: what a litre of tank water replaces, used only to value tank water; a Boond estimate, not the DJB tariff. Confirm both before relying on them.
